T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach with a framework like React or Angular to create a user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on responsive design and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion using a backend framework.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema with tables for problems, categories, and tags. Use indexing for efficient querying.
T3.notes: Normalize the database to avoid redundancy.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a form-based interface for users to submit code, with syntax highlighting and file upload support.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback for syntax errors.

T5.implementation_approach: Use a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security by isolating execution environments.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, activity history, and achievements.
T6.notes: Incorporate visual elements like charts for user stats.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including updating user details and retrieving activity history.

T8.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display top users with sorting and filtering options.
T8.notes: Ensure real-time updates for dynamic leaderboards.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user performance.

T10.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and solutions for problems, with collapsible sections for better user experience.
T10.notes: Ensure hints are displayed progressively to avoid spoilers.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and solutions, including retrieval and updates.
T11.notes: Implement role-based access control for editing.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T12.notes: Focus on edge cases and error handling.

T13.implementation_approach: Simulate code submissions and evaluate the correctness of the evaluation system using test cases.
T13.notes: Test for security vulnerabilities in the sandbox.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionalities, including data retrieval and updates.
T14.notes: Ensure proper handling of authentication and authorization.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify the accuracy and performance of the leaderboard system under different scenarios.
T15.notes: Test for scalability with large datasets.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the functionality of hints and solutions, including progressive hint display.
T16.notes: Ensure proper access control for solutions.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider with CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T17.notes: Ensure scalability, security, and monitoring are in place.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'difficulty': self.difficulty,
            'created_at': self.created_at,
            'updated_at': self.updated_at
        }

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'Pending', 'Accepted', 'Rejected'
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} status={self.status}>"

# app/routes.py
# Layer: assembly
# Purpose: Main routes aggregating all blueprints

from app.controllers.problem_controller import blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Registers all blueprints with the Flask application instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app (example configuration, adjust as necessary)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')
    
    return app

from app import create_app

# Entry point for the application
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance and achievements.
- Hints and Solutions: Provides optional hints and detailed solutions for problems to aid learning.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
